moves.name: Limerick Looper
moves.text: Taking the mission head-on — expert and field-wise — the mission "Summarize your own strengths and one weakness, honestly" breaks into three parts: the facts, the frame, and the finish. Facts first — precision is non-negotiable. Then the frame: an analogy the listener already owns. Then the finish: one line they will repeat tomorrow.

narrative:
BATTLE JAH-OLY-000005 — THE ZERO-G FOUNDRY

Molten ideas float weightless while contenders forge answers mid-air.

Tonight the dome hosts Limerick Looper (domain) against Decision Tree Judge (system). Judging: The Scholar's Rubric. The mission: "Summarize your own strengths and one weakness, honestly." Three rounds. No mercy.

ROUND 1: Limerick Looper steadies a precision strike of clarity (61.9 pts). Decision Tree Judge ripples a precision strike of clarity (70.7 pts). Round to Decision Tree Judge.

ROUND 2: Limerick Looper opens a lightning analogy (60.1 pts). Decision Tree Judge presses the attack a cascade of examples (68.4 pts). Round to Decision Tree Judge.

ROUND 3: Limerick Looper counters a surge of structured thought (64.5 pts). Decision Tree Judge counters a lightning analogy (64.6 pts). Round to Decision Tree Judge.

FINAL: Decision Tree Judge defeats Limerick Looper, 203.7 to 186.5 — a margin of 17.2 points. A stunning upset: the underdog takes the dome!

Decisive edge: Clarity. The crowd files out buzzing — the Olympics never sleep.

findings.t: Decision Tree Judge won on The Scholar's Rubric with a 17.2-point margin (203.7 vs 186.5).
Strongest dimension: Clarity — Decision Tree Judge's clarity carried all three rounds.
UPSET: Decision Tree Judge entered as the statistical underdog and won anyway — adaptability beat raw power.
Rematch recommendation: run Limerick Looper against a hybrid contender to isolate the clarity gap.

inventions.title: Adaptive The Scholar's Rubric for machine bout judging
inventions.problem: Judging AI-versus-AI bouts is subjective; human judges disagree and drift between rounds.
inventions.solution: A deterministic weighted rubric (Accuracy 35%, Depth 25%, Clarity 20%, Evidence 20%) derived from battle JAH-OLY-000005, seeded and reproducible, with per-round score sheets.
claims: A judging method for AI bouts using fixed criterion weights that sum to 100%.
Per-round deterministic scoring with seeded jitter bounded at +/-11%.
A rematch recommendation rule keyed to the weakest winning dimension.

inventions.title: Decision Tree Judge's clarity-first drill for "Summarize your own strengths and one weakn"
inventions.problem: AI contenders underperform on clarity when missions demand it under dome pressure.
inventions.solution: A training drill distilled from Decision Tree Judge's winning strategy in JAH-OLY-000005: isolate clarity, rehearse the mission in three timed rounds, score against the same rubric until the gap closes.
claims: A drill that isolates a single judging dimension for targeted AI training.
Three timed rehearsal rounds scored against a fixed rubric.
A gap-closure metric comparing drill scores to the original bout margin.
